propositions.text: I dismiss this appeal for the reasons that follow.
propositions.quote: I dismiss this appeal for the reasons that follow.

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses this appeal for the reasons that follow.

propositions.text: Ms. XXXX and her sons are Nigerian citizens who had an initial RPD hearing in 2017, which was rejected, but RAD granted their appeal later that year, and RPD re-heard in 2019.
propositions.quote: XXXX XXXX XXXX and her sons, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, are citizens of Nigeria. Ms. XXXX and her sons had an initial hearing before the Refugee Protection Division (RPD) in 2017. The RPD rejected their claims. However, the Refugee Appeal Division (RAD) granted their appeal later that year. Ms. XXXX claims were re-heard by the RPD in 2019.

paragraphs.summary: The court states Ms. XXXX and her sons are Nigerian citizens with initial RPD rejection in 2017, RAD appeal granted later, and RPD re-hearing in 2019.

propositions.text: Ms. XXXX and her sons fear harm or death as sacrifice by in-laws due to family tradition involving first-born sons.
propositions.quote: Ms. XXXX and her sons fear that, if they return to Nigeria, Ms. XXXX in-laws will kill or seriously harm the sons as a sacrifice because Ms. XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX.

propositions.text: Tradition requires first-born son sacrifice when a family member dies; in-laws insist both sons undergo rituals.
propositions.quote: According to Ms. XXXX and her sons, the tradition in her in-laws' family is that the first-born son in the family must be offered up as a sacrifice when a member of the family XXXX XXXX XXXX. For some unknown reason, Ms. XXXX in-laws allegedly insisted that both her sons undergo the rituals.

propositions.text: In-laws consider Ms. XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and would subject her to spiritual cleansing if she returns.
propositions.quote: Ms. XXXX also alleges that her spouse's family considers XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and that they would subject her to spiritual cleansing if she returns to Nigeria.

propositions.text: Family problems started with eldest son's birth; awareness of in-laws' pressure arose when he turned XXXX XXXX XXXX.
propositions.quote: According to Ms. XXXX, her family's problems started with the birth of her eldest son but she only became aware of the pressure being placed by her in-laws when he turned XXXX XXXX XXXX.

propositions.text: Family left Nigeria for US vacation in December XXXX, then came to Canada; spouse returned to Nigeria after threats.
propositions.quote: Ms. XXXX, her spouse, and her sons left Nigeria for the United States (US) for a four-week vacation in December XXXX. Ms. XXXX and her family then came to Canada, allegedly for a vacation that same month. Her spouse returned to Nigeria XXXX XXXX2017 after he allegedly received a threatening phone call from his family.

propositions.text: Spouse visited Canada thrice in 2018 and 2019, returned to Nigeria each time; served divorce papers before RPD re-determination; no response to divorce petition.
propositions.quote: Ms. XXXX spouse returned three times to visit her in Canada in 2018 and 2019 and returned to Nigeria each time. Ms. XXXX alleges that her spouse served her with divorce papers a few months before the RPD's re-determination of this case. Ms. XXXX has not responded to the petition for divorce.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant alleges fear of sacrifice by in-laws, spiritual cleansing threats, family problems starting with eldest son's birth, travel history, and divorce proceedings.

propositions.text: RPD found Ms. XXXX's testimony untrustworthy due to inconsistencies and reactive responses.
propositions.quote: In the decision under appeal, the RPD found that Ms. XXXX testimony was untrustworthy as it found that she could not keep her story straight and, on numerous occasions, her responses were reactive and manufactured.

propositions.text: RPD found insufficient credible evidence to determine Ms. XXXX and sons as refugees or persons in need of protection.
propositions.quote: The RPD found that the cumulative effect of all of the credibility concerns set out in its decision was such that it did not have sufficient credible and trustworthy evidence upon which to base a determination that Ms. XXXX and her sons are Convention refugees or persons in need of protection.

propositions.text: RPD found viable internal flight alternatives in Abuja, Enugu, and/or Port Harcourt for Ms. XXXX and her sons.
propositions.quote: The RPD also found that Ms. XXXX and her sons have a viable internal flight alternative in Abuja, Enugu and/or Port Harcourt.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker found Ms. XXXX's testimony untrustworthy, insufficient credible evidence for refugee status, and viable internal flight alternatives.

propositions.text: My role is to review all evidence and decide if the RPD made the correct decision.
propositions.quote: My role is to look at all the evidence and decide if the RPD made the correct decision.

propositions.text: RPD was correct that Ms. XXXX and sons are neither Convention refugees nor persons in need of protection.
propositions.quote: The RPD was correct in finding that Ms. XXXX and her sons are neither Convention refugees nor persons in need of protection.

propositions.text: Ms. XXXX counsel argues RPD erred on some credibility findings.
propositions.quote: While I agree with Ms. XXXX counsel that the RPD erred with respect to some of its findings relating to credibility,

propositions.text: Findings on which RPD was correct rebut presumption of truthfulness.
propositions.quote: I find that the findings on which the RPD was correct were sufficient to rebut the presumption of truthfulness that applies in this case.

propositions.text: Ms. XXXX's account of leaving Nigeria and risk faced is not credible on balance of probabilities.
propositions.quote: I agree with the RPD that Ms. XXXX account of what led to her and her family to leave Nigeria was not credible, on a balance of probabilities. I also agree with the RPD that Ms. XXXX account of the risk she would face if she and her sons return to Nigeria is not credible.

propositions.text: Ms. XXXX and sons have viable internal flight alternatives in Abuja and/or Enugu.
propositions.quote: Finally, I agree with the RPD that, in any event, Ms. XXXX and her sons would have viable internal flight alternatives, at the very least, in Abuja, and/or Enugu.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds RPD correct that Ms. XXXX and sons are not refugees, despite some RPD credibility errors, and viable internal flight alternatives exist.

propositions.text: RAD only has jurisdiction to hold hearing if new evidence is admitted.
propositions.quote: The RAD only has the jurisdiction to hold a hearing in some cases if it has admitted new evidence.

propositions.text: Ms. XXXX and sons did not seek to admit new evidence and request for in-person hearing is denied.
propositions.quote: Ms. XXXX and her sons did not seek to admit any new evidence and therefore their request for an in-person hearing is denied.

paragraphs.summary: The court states RAD can hold hearings only if new evidence is admitted; Ms. XXXX did not seek new evidence, so hearing request denied.

propositions.text: Counsel argues RPD engaged in microscopic examination to find negative credibility.
propositions.quote: Counsel for Ms. XXXX and her sons argues that the RPD engaged in a microscopic examination of the issues in this case to arrive at its negative credibility findings.

propositions.text: I will address each argument made by counsel in detail below.
propositions.quote: I address each of the arguments made by counsel in detail below.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant's counsel argues RPD's microscopic examination for credibility; the court will address these arguments in detail.

propositions.text: I agree with RPD that there were omissions and inconsistencies in Ms. XXXX's evidence about risks when eldest son turned ten.
propositions.quote: However, I agree with the RPD that there were several omissions and inconsistencies in Ms. XXXX evidence regarding the risk that her family began to face at this time.

paragraphs.summary: The court agrees with RPD that Ms. XXXX's evidence about risks when eldest son turned ten had omissions and inconsistencies.

propositions.text: Counsel argues inconsistency about risk source was omission of peripheral information.
propositions.quote: Counsel argues that an inconsistency in Ms. XXXX evidence regarding the exact source of the risk faced by her sons was simply an omission of peripheral information.

propositions.text: I disagree; Ms. XXXX's written narrative states spouse was XXXX XXXX XXXX and threats arose from spouse's uncle's mockery due to sons not undergoing rituals.
propositions.quote: In the written narrative she submitted with her Basis of Claim form, Ms. XXXX states that her spouse was XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and that he was a candidate XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX of the community. She also states that the threats against her sons arose because her spouse's uncle was the subject of mockery due to the fact that her sons had not undergone certain community rituals.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant's counsel says inconsistency about risk source was peripheral omission; court disagrees, citing written narrative about spouse and uncle's role.

propositions.text: At hearing, Ms. XXXX said risk arose from spouse's brother, not uncle; explained cultural terms blur uncle and elder brother.
propositions.quote: However, at the hearing, Ms. XXXX testified that the risk her family faced arose from the fact that her spouse's brother XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. She later explained that, when she said uncle she was really referring to her spouse's brother who is older and that, in her culture, no distinction is made between elder brothers and uncles.

propositions.text: Even accepting this, Ms. XXXX's evidence about risk source is inconsistent as she did not mention spouse's brother in written narrative but referred to spouse's uncle and community candidate status.
propositions.quote: Even if I accept that this is true, I still agree with the RPD that Ms. XXXX evidence about the source of the risk to her sons was inconsistent as she made no mention of the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX in her written narrative. Instead, as noted above, she referred to her spouse being a candidate for the stool of his community. She also stated that her spouse's uncle (brother) said he had become a subject of mockery among his friends because they thought he could not manage his family and that he might be demoted if the traditional rituals were not performed on Ms. XXXXchildren.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Ms. XXXX's hearing testimony about risk source inconsistent with written narrative, despite cultural explanation.

propositions.text: RPD found Ms. XXXX failed to explain inconsistency satisfactorily, saying she was not herself when writing narrative and it did not cross her mind.
propositions.quote: I agree with the RPD that Ms. XXXX failed to provide a satisfactory explanation for this inconsistency in her evidence as she just testified that she was not herself when she wrote her narrative. Her answer as to why she did not include this information in her amended narrative was also not satisfactory as she simply said it did not cross her mind.

propositions.text: I do not agree that source or reason for risk is a mere detail; it is core to the claim and RPD was justified in focusing on it.
propositions.quote: I do not agree with counsel that the exact source or reason for a claimant's risk of persecution is simply a detail. In my view, it is important information that goes to the core of a claim. I also do not agree with counsel that the RPD was engaging in a microscopic examination by focusing on these matters in addition to the other credibility concerns discussed below.

paragraphs.summary: The court agrees with RPD that Ms. XXXX's explanation for inconsistency was unsatisfactory and that risk source is core, not a mere detail.

propositions.text: Counsel argues RPD erred by applying inappropriate 'memory test' to Ms. XXXX.
propositions.quote: Counsel argued that the RPD erred in subjecting Ms. XXXX to an inappropriate "memory test."

propositions.text: I agree refugee claims should not be decided on inappropriate memory tests but disagree that RPD applied such a test when expecting recall of significant events.
propositions.quote: I certainly agree with counsel that refugee claims should not be determined on the basis of an inappropriate "memory test." However, I disagree with counsel that the RPD was conducting a memory test when it expected Ms. XXXX to remember significant events and threats that occurred around the time that her eldest son turned ten.

propositions.text: Ms. XXXX's written narrative stated in-laws insisted on spiritual cleansing and examined house around eldest son's tenth birthday.
propositions.quote: In her written narrative, Ms. XXXX stated that, around the time that her eldest son turned ten, her spouse's in-laws insisted that she undergo spiritual cleansing because they saw her XXXX XXXX XXXX. Also, her in-laws visited her house to examine the surroundings in order to determine the best way to attack them.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant argues RPD erred with memory test; court agrees memory tests are inappropriate but finds RPD reasonably expected recall of significant events.

propositions.text: Ms. XXXX failed to mention significant threats at hearing, including in-laws' insistence on spiritual cleansing.
propositions.quote: When the RPD asked Ms. XXXX at the hearing what had occurred around the time that her eldest son turned ten, she failed to mention these significant aspects of her claim, in particular that her in-laws were insisting that she undergo spiritual cleansing because they considered her XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX.

propositions.text: It was not a memory test to expect spontaneous recall of serious threats like spiritual cleansing.
propositions.quote: I do not agree that it was a memory test to expect Ms. XXXX to spontaneously remember this serious threat made to her by her in-laws.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Ms. XXXX failed to mention serious threats at hearing and that expecting recall was not a memory test.

propositions.text: Ms. XXXX said she could not remember all events due to many things happening.
propositions.quote: When asked why she had failed to mention this threat in her response to the RPD's questions, Ms. XXXX said that so many things had happened that she could not remember them all.

propositions.text: Being accused of witchcraft and threatened with spiritual cleansing is not a detail one would forget; this undermines credibility.
propositions.quote: I agree with the RPD that being accused of being a witch and being threatened with spiritual cleansing is not a detail one would expect someone to forget, especially since that is the main reason that she personally claimed refugee protection.

propositions.text: RPD's finding that failure to remember this threat negatively affected credibility is agreed with.
propositions.quote: For these reasons, I agree with the RPD's finding that Ms. XXXX's failure to remember this highly significant threat negatively affected the credibility of her account of events in this case.

paragraphs.summary: The court agrees with RPD that forgetting witchcraft accusation and spiritual cleansing threat undermines credibility.

propositions.text: RPD was correct to find omissions and inconsistencies about events when eldest son turned ten adversely affected credibility.
propositions.quote: For the above reasons, the RPD was correct to find that the above omissions and inconsistencies in Ms. XXXX's evidence regarding the events and threats that occurred around the time her eldest son turned ten had an adverse effect on her credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The court agrees RPD correctly found omissions and inconsistencies about events at eldest son's tenth birthday harmed credibility.

propositions.text: Counsel argues RPD misapprehended Ms. XXXX's testimony about when she became aware of in-laws' demands.
propositions.quote: I disagree with counsel that the RPD misapprehended Ms. XXXX testimony or erred in any way in its treatment of Ms. XXXX evidence as to when she became aware of the demands being made by her in-laws.

paragraphs.summary: The court disagrees with counsel that RPD misapprehended Ms. XXXX's testimony about awareness timing of in-laws' demands.

propositions.text: Ms. XXXX testified she only learned of in-laws' demands when spouse told her around son's XXXX XXXX.
propositions.quote: As noted by counsel, Ms. XXXX testified at the hearing that she did not initially know about the demands made by her in-laws that her eldest son undergo certain traditional rituals until her spouse opened up to her about them around the time that her son XXXX XXXX.

propositions.text: She testified this when asked why she did not claim asylum in the US.
propositions.quote: She testified to this when the RPD asked her why she did not make a claim for asylum in the US.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes Ms. XXXX testified she learned of in-laws' demands only when spouse told her around son's XXXX XXXX, explaining US asylum claim timing.

propositions.text: RPD noted Ms. XXXX's testimony conflicts with written narrative stating problems began at eldest son's birth with threats to dedicate him to gods.
propositions.quote: However, the problem with this testimony is that, as noted by the RPD, it is inconsistent with the written narrative submitted by Ms. XXXX. In her written narrative, Ms. XXXX stated that her problems with her in-laws began when her eldest son was born as the in-laws claimed that he had to be dedicated to the gods.

propositions.text: Written narrative states Ms. XXXX and spouse prayed and resisted sacrifices on eldest son.
propositions.quote: She then stated: My spouse and I were persistent and steadfast in our prayers and fasting and we believe (sic) that God would protect our son. My spouse and I did not allow them to perform any sacrifice on our son or with our son.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Ms. XXXX's testimony conflicts with written narrative stating problems began at eldest son's birth and they resisted sacrifices.

propositions.text: Written narrative implies Ms. XXXX was aware of in-laws' threats at eldest son's birth, including her own efforts to pray and resist.
propositions.quote: This part of her written narrative clearly implies that she was aware of her in-laws' threats at the time that her eldest son was born as she includes herself in the efforts to pray for him and to disallow the sacrifices.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the written narrative implies Ms. XXXX was aware of threats at eldest son's birth and resisted them.

propositions.text: Ms. XXXX explained inconsistency by saying spouse did not initially tell her and she did not know until son XXXX XXXX; prayed for son's safety.
propositions.quote: When asked to explain the inconsistency between her written narrative and her testimony as to when she became aware of the threats being made by her in-laws, Ms. XXXX kept stating that her spouse did not initially tell her about the threats and that she did not know about them until her son XXXX XXXX. She also said that many things happened and that she and her spouse prayed for the safety of their son.

propositions.text: RPD found these explanations unsatisfactory for inconsistency between testimony and written narrative about awareness timing.
propositions.quote: I agree with the RPD that these were not satisfactory explanations for the inconsistency between Ms. XXXX's testimony and her written narrative as to when she first found out about the threats being made by her in-laws.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Ms. XXXX's explanations for inconsistency about awareness timing unsatisfactory, agreeing with RPD.

propositions.text: Inconsistency in Ms. XXXX's evidence about threats from in-laws after a certain event.
propositions.quote: this same inconsistency arose in Ms. XXXX's evidence regarding threats the in-laws made after the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX

propositions.text: Ms. XXXX testified she was unaware of threats at that time but her written narrative says otherwise.
propositions.quote: While Ms. XXXX testified that she was not aware of the threats being made by her in-laws at that time, she states in her written narrative that her spouse's uncle (brother) invited her and her spouse to his village to talk to them about initiating the child.

propositions.text: Written narrative states she and spouse told uncle they were not interested and believed in Christianity.
propositions.quote: She states in her written narrative that she and her spouse told him that they were not interested and that they believed in Christianity.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds inconsistency in Ms. XXXX's evidence about threats from in-laws after a certain event, noting her testimony and written narrative conflict.

propositions.text: Ms. XXXX's explanation for inconsistency is that she was not involved in meetings and unaware of children's jeopardy then.
propositions.quote: Ms. XXXX replied that, although she went to the village with her spouse, she was not involved in the meetings and she did not know that her children were in jeopardy at that time.

propositions.text: This explanation conflicts with her written narrative stating both were involved in telling uncle they were not interested.
propositions.quote: her testimony are inconsistent with her written narrative which clearly states that she and her spouse were both involved in telling the uncle/brother that they were not interested in subjecting their son to the initiation.

propositions.text: Written narrative mentions many meetings where uncle tried to convince them to perform sacrifices.
propositions.quote: there were many more instances or meetings in which her spouse's uncle/brother tried to convince them (that is, her and her spouse) XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and that all necessary sacrifices must be carried out.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Ms. XXXX's explanation for inconsistency conflicts with her written narrative showing involvement in meetings and threats.

propositions.text: Disagrees with counsel that RPD's timing assessment was microscopic; timing is significant to credibility.
propositions.quote: I do not agree with counsel that the RPD's assessment of the issue of when Ms. XXXX became aware of the threats being made by her in-laws was microscopic.

propositions.text: Ms. XXXX likely adjusted testimony to reduce delay between awareness and departure, diminishing credibility.
propositions.quote: Ms. XXXX was most probably adjusting her testimony at the hearing to make it seem like there had been less of a delay between her awareness of the threats made by her in-laws and her departure from Nigeria. I find that this diminishes her credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the timing of Ms. XXXX's awareness significant and that she likely adjusted testimony, diminishing credibility.

propositions.text: Disagrees with counsel that RPD erred in finding credibility compromised due to inconsistent ritual descriptions.
propositions.quote: I do not agree with counsel that the RPD erred in finding that Ms. XXXX credibility was compromised due to her inconsistent description of what was involved in the initiation, sacrifice and dedication rituals she described in her written narrative.

propositions.text: Written narrative describes rituals involving evil forest, concoction, and swearing to shrine.
propositions.quote: Ms. XXXX stated that the rituals entailed going into the evil forest with the chief priest and living there for seven days. She also said it also involved taking a concoction and swearing to the village shrine.

propositions.text: At hearing, Ms. XXXX said sacrifice involved killing her son, inconsistent with narrative.
propositions.quote: when the RPD asked her what the dedication or sacrifice involved, she said her son would be killed.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Ms. XXXX's inconsistent ritual descriptions diminish her credibility, rejecting counsel's argument of no error.

propositions.text: Counsel argues testimony not inconsistent; threats explained in narrative.
propositions.quote: In the appeal memorandum, counsel argues that Ms. XXXX testimony was not inconsistent as she stated in her written narrative that her spouse's uncle/brother told them that, if they did not bring her son for the sacrifice, the son would die in a mysterious way or they could come take him by force.

propositions.text: This explanation addresses threats but not inconsistency about what sacrifice entails.
propositions.quote: this portion speaks to the threats allegedly made by the in-laws if the son was not brought to them for the sacrifice. It still does not explain the inconsistency in Ms. XXXX evidence as to what the sacrifice itself would entail.

propositions.text: Testimony says sacrifice is killing son; narrative does not mention killing as sacrifice.
propositions.quote: In her testimony she said that the sacrifice entailed killing her son as a sacrifice to the gods whereas there is no mention of such killing as a sacrifice to the gods in her written narrative.

paragraphs.summary: Counsel argues no inconsistency about threats, but court finds inconsistency remains about what sacrifice entails.

propositions.text: Agrees with RPD that Ms. XXXX likely embellished claim by testifying sacrifice involved killing son.
propositions.quote: I agree with the RPD that Ms. XXXX was likely embellishing her claim by testifying at the hearing that the sacrifice being asked of her in-laws entailed the killing of her son as a sacrifice to the gods.

propositions.text: Ms. XXXX's failure to provide clear, consistent evidence diminishes credibility of harm risk account.
propositions.quote: Her failure to provide clear and consistent evidence about what is involved in these rituals, and her apparent embellishment at the hearing, diminish the credibility of her account of the harm that she and her sons risk if they return to Nigeria.

paragraphs.summary: The court agrees Ms. XXXX likely embellished testimony about sacrifice, diminishing credibility of harm risk account.

propositions.text: Counsel argues RPD erred in drawing negative inference about who Ms. XXXX feared in spouse's family.
propositions.quote: I agree with counsel that the RPD erred in drawing a negative inference due to the inconsistency in Ms. XXXX evidence as to who exactly she feared in her spouse's family.

propositions.text: Ms. XXXX satisfactorily explained fearing mostly brother but also whole family.
propositions.quote: she provided a satisfactory explanation for this differing testimony when she said that she mostly feared the brother but also feared the rest of the family.

paragraphs.summary: Counsel argues RPD erred on fear inconsistency; court finds Ms. XXXX's explanation satisfactory.

propositions.text: Counsel argues RPD erred in finding credibility diminished by failure to testify to key April 2016 incident.
propositions.quote: I do not agree with counsel that the RPD erred in finding that Ms. XXXX credibility was diminished by her failure to testify to a significant incident which allegedly occurred in April 2016 and which was the key event that allegedly caused her family to leave Nigeria.

paragraphs.summary: Counsel argues RPD erred on credibility due to failure to testify key incident; court disagrees.

propositions.text: Ms. XXXX's written narrative recounts 2014 events and April 2016 ultimatum from spouse's uncle.
propositions.quote: In her written narrative, Ms. XXXX recounted events that occurred in 2014, around the time her eldest son XXXX XXXX. She then alleged that, in April 2016, her spouse's uncle issued an ultimatum that her spouse must either bring the son to him or he would forcibly abduct him.

propositions.text: Written narrative says pressure became unbearable then and family decided to travel to US and Canada.
propositions.quote: In her written narrative, Ms. XXXX stated that it was at this point that the pressure became unbearable and she and her spouse decided to travel to the US and then to Canada.

propositions.text: At hearing, Ms. XXXX said no further problems from in-laws between 2014 and departure in 2016.
propositions.quote: When the RPD asked Ms. XXXX at the hearing whether she had had any further problems from her in-laws between the time her eldest XXXX XXXX XXXX in 2014 and the time she left Nigeria in XXXX2016, Ms. XXXX said she had not.

propositions.text: Ms. XXXX said personally no problems with in-laws and spouse did not tell her of issues.
propositions.quote: Ms. XXXX said that, personally, she had no problems with the in-laws. She then reiterated that her spouse had not told her about anything until her eldest son XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX

propositions.text: Ms. XXXX contradicted herself about problems after 2014, saying she had no problems but then clarifying she meant personally.
propositions.quote: Ms. XXXX later contradicted herself by saying that she had not said that there were no problems but instead that she herself had not had any problems.

propositions.text: When pressed, Ms. XXXX said she was unaware of what occurred after 2014 and spouse did not tell her.
propositions.quote: she just said that she was not aware of anything and that, if her spouse went through something with his family, he did not tell her.

propositions.text: Ms. XXXX said she expected to explain everything orally before RPD but did not do so.
propositions.quote: Ms. XXXX said that it had been a while since she wrote her narrative and that she believed that she would have the opportunity to explain everything orally before the RPD.

paragraphs.summary: The court recounts Ms. XXXX's narrative and hearing testimony about events and ultimatum between 2014 and 2016.

propositions.text: RPD's finding that Ms. XXXX's explanation for not explaining orally was unsatisfactory is agreed with.
propositions.quote: I agree with the RPD that this is not a satisfactory explanation for why Ms. XXXX in fact did not explain everything orally to the RPD when asked directly about what occurred between 2014 and the time she and her family left Nigeria over two years later.

propositions.text: Counsel blames failure to testify on Ms. XXXX's mental health issues.
propositions.quote: In the appeal memorandum, counsel seeks to blame Ms. XXXX's failure to testify to the ultimatum that made her family leave Nigeria on her XXXX XXXX.

propositions.text: Ms. XXXX did not provide mental health explanation at hearing.
propositions.quote: I note that Ms. XXXX did not provide this explanation at the hearing.

propositions.text: Psychological report states trauma can cause memory problems but ultimatum was key event, not detail.
propositions.quote: While the XXXX XXXX states that persons exposed to trauma often have problems "retrieving specific details from the past," the ultimatum was not a detail but instead the key event that made the pressure unbearable and that made Ms. XXXX and her spouse realize they and their sons were no longer safe in Nigeria.

paragraphs.summary: The court agrees RPD that Ms. XXXX's explanation for not testifying orally is unsatisfactory and mental health does not explain it.

propositions.text: Psychological report does not support argument that mental health explains failure to remember key incident.
propositions.quote: I do not agree with counsel that the psychological report supports the argument that Ms. XXXX's mental health condition would adequately explain her failure to spontaneously remember the key incident that led to her family's departure from Nigeria.

propositions.text: Expecting Ms. XXXX to remember key incident was not an improper memory test.
propositions.quote: I also do not agree with counsel that expecting Ms. XXXX to remember this key incident was an improper memory test.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds psychological report does not support mental health excuse and memory test was proper.

propositions.text: RPD properly questioned Ms. XXXX about suspicious timing coincidence of arrival and threats.
propositions.quote: I do not agree with counsel that it was improper for the RPD to question Ms. XXXX about the coincidence in timing between her family's arrival in Canada and the demands that her spouse's family made shortly thereafter.

propositions.text: RPD had obligation to allow Ms. XXXX to address concerns about suspicious timing.
propositions.quote: the RPD had the obligation to provide Ms. XXXX with a chance to address its concerns about this coincidence in timing.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds RPD properly questioned Ms. XXXX about suspicious timing and gave her chance to respond.

propositions.text: RPD did not err in drawing negative inference from timing coincidence of threats and arrival.
propositions.quote: I also do not agree with counsel that the RPD erred in drawing a negative inference based on the coincidence in timing.

propositions.text: Ms. XXXX alleged ultimatum in April 2016, no action for six months, then threats resumed after arrival in Canada.
propositions.quote: Ms. XXXX alleged that her in-laws gave her spouse an ultimatum in April 2016, then took no action for the six months it took before they left Nigeria in XXXX XXXX, and then suddenly resumed their threats a couple of weeks after Ms. XXXX and her family arrived in Canada.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds RPD did not err in negative inference from timing coincidence of threats and arrival.

propositions.text: Negative credibility findings cannot be based solely on suspicious timing coincidences.
propositions.quote: In my view, the RPD cannot simply base a negative credibility finding on suspicious coincidences in timing.

propositions.text: If timing coincidence was only concern, it would not rebut presumption of truthfulness.
propositions.quote: If the coincidence in timing in this case had been the only credibility concern arising from Ms. XXXX's evidence, it likely would not have been of such significance as to rebut the presumption of truthfulness.

propositions.text: Timing coincidence was one of several credibility concerns; RPD did not err in relying on it contextually.
propositions.quote: this coincidence in timing was not the only credibility concern in this case. Credibility assessments are contextual exercises based on a variety of factors. I do not find that the RPD erred in placing some reliance upon this coincidence of events as part of its overall credibility assessment in this case.

paragraphs.summary: The court states timing alone cannot discredit, but RPD properly considered it among other concerns.

propositions.text: Counsel argues RPD failed to consider spouse's social and cultural background in negative inference about trips to Nigeria.
propositions.quote: I do not agree with counsel that the RPD failed to view the actions of Ms. XXXX spouse from his social and cultural background when it drew a negative inference as to credibility based on the fact that Ms. XXXX's spouse returned to Nigeria three times during a time when his life was supposedly also at risk at the hands of his family members.

paragraphs.summary: Counsel argues RPD erred by not considering spouse's social and cultural background regarding trips to Nigeria.

propositions.text: Ms. XXXX said spouse returned to Nigeria for business and cannot live abroad.
propositions.quote: When the RPD asked Ms. XXXX why her spouse would return to Nigeria if his life was at risk there, she replied that he could not remain in Canada because he has business in Nigeria and he cannot live abroad.

propositions.text: Spouse's trips raise credibility concerns about risk to life claim during that period.
propositions.quote: I agree with the RPD that her spouse's three trips to Canada and back to Nigeria between December 2016 and December 2018 raised concerns regarding the credibility of Ms. XXXX's claim that she, her spouse, and her sons faced a risk to their lives at the hands of her in-laws during this period of time.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds spouse's trips raise credibility concerns about risk to life claim during that period.

propositions.text: Counsel offers explanation for spouse's trips and argues RPD failed to consider social and cultural background.
propositions.quote: In the appeal memorandum, counsel seeks to provide a further explanation for the trips that Ms. XXXX spouse made between Canada and Nigeria XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. However, this explanation has no actual basis in Ms. XXXX's testimony as Ms. XXXX did not provide the explanation when asked about her spouse's actions by the RPD. Counsel argues that Ms. XXXX spouse was more concerned with his family's safety than his own and that he wanted to resolve things with his family. Counsel argues that the RPD failed to view the actions of Ms. XXXX's spouse from his social and cultural background.

propositions.text: Court disagrees with counsel's argument about social and cultural background consideration.
propositions.quote: I disagree.

paragraphs.summary: Counsel argues for social and cultural context for spouse's trips; court disagrees.

propositions.text: In-laws continued threats after 2017 hearing; spouse came to Canada twice in 2018 and returned to Nigeria each time.
propositions.quote: According to Ms. XXXX's amended narrative, her in-laws continued to threaten her spouse even after the first RPD hearing in 2017. The documentary evidence shows that her spouse came to Canada twice in 2018 and Ms. XXXX testified that he came to visit in XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, he returned to Nigeria each time, a country where he is allegedly at risk of death, rather than claiming asylum in Canada as his wife and children had done.

propositions.text: Ms. XXXX's lack of concern for spouse's risk diminishes her credibility.
propositions.quote: her apparent lack of concern for the risk that her spouse was taking in travelling back and forth between Canada and Nigeria was incompatible with her account of the danger to life that he faced in Nigeria and her credibility was diminished as a result.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds spouse's repeated returns to Nigeria and Ms. XXXX's lack of concern diminish her credibility.

propositions.text: Counsel argues RPD erred in finding failure to explain failure to claim asylum in US diminished credibility.
propositions.quote: I do not agree with counsel that the RPD erred in finding that Ms. XXXX had failed to provide a satisfactory explanation for her failure to claim asylum during her time in the US and that this diminished the credibility of her account of the risk she and her sons faced in Nigeria.

paragraphs.summary: Counsel argues RPD erred on credibility due to failure to explain failure to claim asylum in US; court disagrees.

propositions.text: Ms. XXXX testified she never intended to claim asylum in US and arrived in Canada before problems started.
propositions.quote: When the RPD asked Ms. XXXX why she had not claimed asylum in the US, she testified that it was never her intention to claim in the US. On the second hearing date, she said that she did not claim asylum in the US because the people her family were staying with in the US had left the country for a vacation and that she had arrived in Canada "before the problem started."

paragraphs.summary: The court recounts Ms. XXXX's testimony about not claiming asylum in US due to intention and timing.

propositions.text: Reasons for not claiming asylum in the US were unsatisfactory as per RPD
propositions.quote: I agree with the RPD that the reasons that Ms. XXXX gave for not claiming asylum in the US were not satisfactory.

propositions.text: Presence of family in US irrelevant to asylum claim if lives were in danger
propositions.quote: the presence or non-presence of the family she was staying with in the US has no bearing on her ability to claim asylum if her and her son's lives were truly in danger

propositions.text: Claim that problem had not started contradicts testimony about problems since 2014 or earlier
propositions.quote: her claim that the problem had not started contradicts the rest of her testimony which was that the problems with her spouse's family began in 2014 or even earlier

propositions.text: Written narrative states situation became unbearable by 2016
propositions.quote: in her written narrative, Ms. XXXX stated that things had become unbearable by that point

paragraphs.summary: Court agrees with RPD that reasons for not claiming asylum in US were unsatisfactory and inconsistent with testimony and narrative.

propositions.text: Counsel argues Ms. XXXX and children could not stay in US due to lack of support
propositions.quote: In the appeal memorandum, counsel argues that Ms. XXXX and her children could not stay in the US because they did not have any support there.

propositions.text: Unclear what counsel means by relying on persons 'already in the system'
propositions.quote: It is unclear what counsel means by this last part of the sentence.

propositions.text: Ms. XXXX did not testify about relying on persons 'already in the system'
propositions.quote: Ms. XXXX did not say anything in her testimony about having to rely on other persons who were "already in the system."

propositions.text: Explanation suggests asylum claim in Canada due to support there, contradicting testimony of vacation intent
propositions.quote: this explanation appears to suggest that Ms. XXXX and her sons claimed asylum in Canada because they could rely on persons who were already in the system here. This would contradict her testimony that she and her family merely came to Canada for a vacation and they had no intention of claiming refugee status here.

paragraphs.summary: Respondent argues lack of support in US; court finds counsel's explanation unclear and contradicts Ms. XXXX's testimony.

propositions.text: Failure to claim asylum in US and inconsistent explanations negatively affect credibility of risk claim
propositions.quote: This failure to claim asylum in the US and the inconsistencies in the explanations given for it give rise to a negative inference regarding the credibility of the risk that Ms. XXXX and her family alleged in this case.

paragraphs.summary: Court concludes failure to claim asylum in US and inconsistent explanations undermine credibility of risk claim.

propositions.text: Counsel argues three-week delay in claiming asylum in Canada should not affect credibility
propositions.quote: I agree with counsel that the RPD erred in finding that Ms. XXXX's three-week delay in claiming asylum in Canada adversely affected her credibility.

propositions.text: Three-week delay is not necessarily excessive
propositions.quote: I agree with counsel that a three-week delay is not necessarily excessive.

paragraphs.summary: Court agrees with counsel that three-week delay in claiming asylum in Canada is not excessive and should not affect credibility.

propositions.text: RPD correctly found many documents had irregularities and gave them little weight
propositions.quote: I agree with the RPD's finding that little weight should be given to many of the documents submitted by Ms. XXXX and her sons due to irregularities found on the face of the documents.

propositions.text: Counsel argues RPD's findings on some documents were microscopic
propositions.quote: I agree with counsel that the RPD's findings were microscopic with respect to some of the documents.

paragraphs.summary: Court agrees with RPD that many documents had irregularities but notes counsel's argument that findings were microscopic on some.

propositions.text: Counsel argues RPD erred by relying on spelling and typographical errors to discount two medical reports
propositions.quote: I agree with counsel that the RPD erred in basing itself on spelling and typographical errors to give little weight to two medical reports stating that Ms. XXXX's husband had XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX2017.

propositions.text: Other irregularities exist on face of medical reports
propositions.quote: However, I note that there are other irregularities on the face of the documents.

propositions.text: Two medical reports are essentially the same but differ in date and appearance
propositions.quote: Both documents essentially say the same thing and therefore it is unclear why both were submitted and why one would be dated March 7, 2017 and the other March 31, 2017. Despite being dated the same month, the documents look completely different one from the other.

paragraphs.summary: Court notes counsel's argument on spelling errors but finds other irregularities and inconsistencies in medical reports.

propositions.text: Even ignoring irregularities, medical reports do not offset serious credibility issues
propositions.quote: even if I were to overlook these irregularities, I find that any weight that could be accorded to these medical reports does not make up for the serious credibility issues detailed above arising from Ms. XXXX's evidence in this case.

propositions.text: Medical reports do not assist in repairing credibility problems
propositions.quote: the reports do not assist in repairing any of the credibility problems detailed above.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds medical reports do not overcome serious credibility issues in Ms. XXXX's evidence.

propositions.text: Counsel argues RPD erred in giving little weight to unsigned affidavit with court stamps
propositions.quote: I disagree with counsel that the RPD erred in giving little weight to this affidavit because the declarant did not sign the affidavit. Counsel argues that the fact that the affidavit bears the stamps of the court means that it is presumed genuine.

propositions.text: Unsigned affidavit is not credible despite court stamps
propositions.quote: Even if that were the case, this presumption is rebutted by the fact that there was no signature on it. It is not credible that a court would commission an affidavit that was not actually signed by the affiant.

paragraphs.summary: Court rejects counsel's argument and finds unsigned affidavit not credible despite court stamps.

propositions.text: Police extract date error could be overlooked due to Nigeria's status
propositions.quote: Even if I were to agree with counsel that the error in the date on the police extract should be overlooked due to the fact that Nigeria is a third world country,

propositions.text: Any weight of police extract outweighed by credibility problems in Ms. XXXX's account
propositions.quote: I do find that any weight that could be given to the report outweigh the credibility problems relating to Ms. XXXX's account of the events that led her to claim refugee protection.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds police extract date error could be overlooked but its weight is outweighed by credibility problems in Ms. XXXX's account.

propositions.text: RPD found limited weight should be given to emails between Ms. XXXX and spouse
propositions.quote: I agree with the RPD that any weight that could be given to the emails between Ms. XXXX and her spouse is limited.

propositions.text: Emails appear sent specifically for evidence use and are not credible
propositions.quote: the emails appear to have been sent for the specific purpose of being used as evidence in this case... I do not find it credible that Ms. XXXX would start an email to his wife in this way.

propositions.text: Emails should be accorded no weight and do not outweigh credibility issues
propositions.quote: Therefore, they should be accorded no weight. Any weight that could be given to the emails does not outweigh the credibility issues detailed above.

paragraphs.summary: Court agrees with RPD that emails were likely fabricated for evidence and should be given no weight.

propositions.text: Counsel argues RPD erred in giving little weight to documents about alleged assault
propositions.quote: I do not agree with counsel that the RPD erred giving little weight to the documents relating to the alleged assault of Ms. XXXX's spouse and XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX.

paragraphs.summary: Court disagrees with counsel and supports RPD's decision to give little weight to assault-related documents.

propositions.text: RPD noted affidavit omitted mention of family killing over ritual dispute
propositions.quote: the RPD noted that the affidavit by Ms. XXXX spouse failed to mention that XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX.

propositions.text: Counsel argues affidavits should be considered for what they say, not omit
propositions.quote: While it is true, as noted by counsel, that affidavits should generally be considered for what they say rather than what they do not say, this is not a hard and fast rule.

propositions.text: Federal Court allows negative credibility inference for omission of material information
propositions.quote: The Federal Court has found it appropriate to draw a negative credibility inference in relation to a document that omits to mention material information.

propositions.text: Omission of family killing is material and justifies negative credibility inference
propositions.quote: One would certainly expect that, if the family of Ms. XXXX spouse killed his father over the dispute over the rituals, he would have thought it important to make some mention of it in his affidavit.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds omission of family killing in affidavit material and justifies negative credibility inference, despite counsel's argument.

propositions.text: RPD found same address on affidavits of spouse and neighbour, unexplained by Ms. XXXX
propositions.quote: the same address was provided on the affidavit sworn by Ms. XXXX spouse and the affidavit sworn by an alleged neighbour. When the RPD asked Ms. XXXX why the affidavits indicated that the men lived at the same address, she had no explanation.

propositions.text: Counsel did not contest RPD's finding on same address irregularity
propositions.quote: Counsel did not contest the RPD's finding that this was a further reason to grant little weight to the documents.

propositions.text: Finding of same address irregularity was correct and justifies little weight to documents
propositions.quote: This finding by the RPD was correct. One would not expect both Ms. XXXX spouse and his neighbour to live at the same address. If there were an explanation for this same address, it should have been easy for Ms. XXXX to provide it at the hearing.

paragraphs.summary: Court agrees with RPD that same address on affidavits is irregular and justifies little weight to documents.

propositions.text: Even if other reasons to discount documents accepted, irregularity and omission suffice to give little weight
propositions.quote: Even if I were to agree with the arguments made by counsel regarding the additional reasons provided by the RPD for discounting the weight accorded to these documents, I find that the irregularity and omission discussed above were sufficient to accord the documents little weight in terms of establishing a forward-looking risk in this case.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds irregularity and omission alone justify giving little weight to documents for risk assessment.

propositions.text: Counsel argues RPD erred in giving little weight to psychological report
propositions.quote: I do not agree with counsel that the RPD erred in giving little weight to the psychological report submitted by Ms. XXXX in the assessment of the credibility issues described above.

paragraphs.summary: Court disagrees with counsel and supports RPD's decision to give little weight to psychological report.

propositions.text: Psychological report states Ms. XXXX met criteria but only based on interview, no independent testing
propositions.quote: The report states that Ms. XXXX satisfied the criteria XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. ... the report only states that it was based on an interview of Ms. XXXX. It makes no mention of any independent testing.

propositions.text: RPD correctly questioned reliability of report due to Ms. XXXX's lack of credibility
propositions.quote: Given that the RPD correctly found Ms. XXXX not credible in relation to key aspects of her claim, the RPD was correct to question the reliability of the opinions in the report as they were based on an account of events that the RPD found not credible in several key respects.

propositions.text: Counsel argues Ms. XXXX's psychological state impacted testimony and memory
propositions.quote: While counsel argues that Ms. XXXX was experiencing XXXX XXXX at the hearing that impacted her testimony and memory recall, the XXXX XXXX does not provide support for this argument.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds psychological report based only on interview and questions its reliability given Ms. XXXX's credibility issues.

propositions.text: Difference between genuine trauma memory loss and intermittent memory loss to explain inconsistencies
propositions.quote: there is a difference between genuine memory loss due to trauma and loss of memory that arises intermittently to explain certain lacunae or inconsistencies in testimony.

propositions.text: Ms. XXXX blamed psychological issues only for few inconsistencies, not key risk events
propositions.quote: Ms. XXXX did not blame very many inconsistencies on any psychological issues. The only times she blamed her state of mind were when she gave inconsistent testimony about the source of the risk she and her family faced and when she failed to testify about the ultimatum given by her brother-in-law in April 2016.

propositions.text: Key risk events are not minor details but central to Ms. XXXX's account
propositions.quote: While the psychological report states that persons exposed to trauma often have problems "retrieving specific details from the past," neither the reason for the risk faced by Ms. XXXX nor the key event that led her and her family to flee Nigeria are details.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds Ms. XXXX's psychological issues do not explain key inconsistencies in her account of risk events.

propositions.text: Psychological report does not establish that evidence problems relate to psychological issues
propositions.quote: I do not find that the psychological report establishes that the problems with Ms. XXXX evidence were likely related to any psychological issues she may have been experiencing at the time of the hearing.

paragraphs.summary: Court concludes psychological report does not explain problems with Ms. XXXX's evidence.

propositions.text: RPD erred on some factors but was correct on many others affecting credibility
propositions.quote: While the RPD did err with respect to some of the factors it relied upon to find Ms. XXXX not credible, it was also correct to find that many other factors adversely affected the credibility of Ms. XXXX account of events.

propositions.text: Credibility concerns identified by RPD suffice to rebut presumption of truthfulness
propositions.quote: In my view, the factors set out above on which the RPD was correct were sufficient to rebut the presumption of truthfulness in this case.

propositions.text: Cumulative credibility concerns mean Ms. XXXX and sons failed to establish refugee or protection status
propositions.quote: Overall, the cumulative effect of the credibility concerns correctly identified by the RPD is that Ms. XXXX and her sons failed to credibly establish that they are either Convention refugees or persons in need of protection.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds cumulative credibility concerns justify rejecting Ms. XXXX's refugee or protection claim.

propositions.text: Even if risk established, RPD correctly found viable internal flight alternative in Abuja or Enugu
propositions.quote: even if I were to find that Ms. XXXX and her sons had credibly established that they would be at risk of persecution or serious harm if they were to return to their home town, I find that the RPD was correct to find that they have a viable internal flight alternative in Abuja or Enugu.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds RPD correctly identified viable internal flight alternative even if risk were established.

propositions.text: The onus is on Ms. XXXX and her sons to prove no viable internal flight alternative in Nigeria.
propositions.quote: The onus is on Ms. XXXX and her sons to demonstrate that they do not have a viable internal flight alternative in Nigeria.

propositions.text: Internal flight alternative test has two prongs: no serious persecution risk and unreasonableness of conditions.
propositions.quote: The two-pronged test to establish an internal flight alternative is the following.12 (1) The decision-maker must be satisfied on the balance of probabilities that the Appellants would not face a serious possibility of persecution... (2) The conditions... must be such that it would not be unreasonable...

propositions.text: Unreasonableness threshold requires conditions jeopardizing claimant's life and safety.
propositions.quote: The threshold for unreasonableness is a very high one and requires nothing less than the existence of conditions that would jeopardize the life and safety of a claimant.13

paragraphs.summary: The court states the two-pronged internal flight alternative test and places the onus on Ms. XXXX and her sons to prove no viable alternative.

propositions.text: The court disagrees with counsel's arguments that the RPD erred on the first prong of the internal flight alternative test.
propositions.quote: I do not agree with any of the arguments made by counsel as to why he believes the RPD erred in the application of the first prong of the internal flight alternative test.

paragraphs.summary: The court rejects counsel's arguments that the RPD erred on the first prong of the internal flight alternative test.

propositions.text: Counsel argues Ms. XXXX's brother-in-law could track her using her Bank Verification Number (BVN).
propositions.quote: Counsel relies on evidence in the National Documentation Package to argue that it is "not inconceivable" that Ms. XXXX brother-in-law would be able to use her Bank Verification Number (BVN) to track her down if she were to return to Nigeria.

propositions.text: 'Not inconceivable' is a lower standard than serious possibility of persecution; evidence does not establish serious possibility of tracking via BVN.
propositions.quote: However, "not inconceivable" is a far lower standard than a serious possibility of persecution, and I agree with the RPD that the available evidence does not establish a serious possibility that Ms. XXXX brother-in-law would be capable of tracking her down using her BVN number.

propositions.text: RPD applied proper standard of proof, not western standards, regarding BVN tracking argument.
propositions.quote: I do not agree that the RPD was approaching counsel's arguments regarding the BVN using western standards. It was instead applying the proper standard of proof to find that... Ms. XXXX's brother-in-law would not be able to track her down that way.

paragraphs.summary: Counsel argues tracking via BVN is possible; court finds evidence insufficient and RPD applied correct standard of proof.

propositions.text: National Documentation shows some bank fraud but insufficient evidence brother-in-law has contacts to access BVN and track Ms. XXXX.
propositions.quote: The National Documentation Package for Nigeria does indicate that there have been some instances of fraud as syndicates attempt to access people's bank accounts and defraud them. However, there was insufficient evidence to establish that Ms. XXXX's brother-in-law has the kind of contacts or resources that would enable him to get access to her BVN and track her down...

paragraphs.summary: Court finds insufficient evidence brother-in-law could access BVN to track Ms. XXXX despite some bank fraud instances.

propositions.text: Counsel argues RPD imposed too high a proof standard requiring definitive proof of tracking ability.
propositions.quote: I also do not agree with counsel that the RPD imposed on Ms. XXXX and her sons a higher standard of proof than appropriate by requiring them to provide definitive proof that their agent of persecution would be able to locate them...

propositions.text: RPD required persuasive evidence on balance of probabilities, not definitive proof, to establish serious possibility of persecution.
propositions.quote: The RPD did not require definitive proof but it did correctly require some kind of persuasive evidence to establish the facts being alleged... and to establish that there was a serious possibility of Ms. XXXX's brother-in-law persecuting Ms. XXXX and her sons...

paragraphs.summary: Counsel argues RPD required too high proof; court finds RPD required persuasive evidence, not definitive proof.

propositions.text: RPD found no evidence besides Ms. XXXX's testimony that brother-in-law was retired police with tracking connections.
propositions.quote: In this case, the RPD found that there was no evidence, other than Ms. XXXX testimony, that her brother-in-law was a retired police officer who had connections that would permit him to track Ms. XXXX and her sons down all over Nigeria.

propositions.text: RPD found police likely ineffective in finding claimants even if brother-in-law had authority to enlist them.
propositions.quote: The RPD also found that, in any event, even if Ms. XXXX brother-in-law did have the authority to engage members of the Nigerian police force all over Nigeria to search for Ms. XXXX and her sons, the police would likely be ineffective in finding the claimants.

propositions.text: Counsel challenges only police effectiveness finding, citing National Documentation on police presence at airports and crime reporters.
propositions.quote: In the appeal memorandum, counsel does not challenge the first finding but only challenges the second by seeking to rely on evidence in the National Documentation Package that the Nigerian police has a command at airports and also has crime reporters.

propositions.text: RPD correctly found insufficient credible evidence brother-in-law was retired police able to enlist police nationwide to track claimants.
propositions.quote: In my view, the RPD did not need to make the alternative finding about the effectiveness of the police force, as it was correct to find that there was insufficient credible evidence in this case to establish that Ms. XXXX brother-in-law was a retired police officer who would be able to enlist the services of police all over Nigeria...

paragraphs.summary: RPD found no evidence brother-in-law was retired police with tracking ability; court agrees RPD correctly found insufficient evidence.

propositions.text: Counsel argues RPD erred by saying Ms. XXXX need not inform brother-in-law of return, equating to requiring hiding.
propositions.quote: Finally, I do not agree that the RPD erred in noting that Ms. XXXX had no need to advise her brother-in-law or any of her in-laws of her return to the country. Counsel argues that this is tantamount to requiring her to remain in hiding.

propositions.text: Refraining from informing agents of persecution is not living in hiding; no evidence brother-in-law would know return without being told.
propositions.quote: I do not agree. Refraining from advising your agents of persecution of your return to your home country is not tantamount to living in hiding... She and her sons would not be required to live in hiding... They simply would have to refrain from informing the agents of persecution where they are.

paragraphs.summary: Counsel argues RPD required hiding; court finds not informing agents is not hiding and no evidence brother-in-law would know return otherwise.

propositions.text: Counsel relies on case where claimant was expected to avoid family needing support as rape victim.
propositions.quote: The case on which counsel seeks to rely is distinguishable as in that case, the RPD expected the claimant not to have any contact with her family when she would require their support due to being a rape victim.14

propositions.text: Present case differs as no valid reason for Ms. XXXX to inform in-laws of return or whereabouts.
propositions.quote: In the present case, there was no valid reason for Ms. XXXX to inform her in-laws or anyone who would inform them of her and her son's whereabouts.

paragraphs.summary: Counsel cites a case about avoiding family contact; court finds present case differs with no need to inform in-laws.

propositions.text: Court finds RPD correct in first prong internal flight alternative analysis after reviewing all evidence.
propositions.quote: For all these reasons, I do not agree with the reasons given by counsel as to why he believes the RPD erred in applying the first prong of the internal flight alternative analysis. Having reviewed all of the evidence in this case, I find that the RPD was correct in its analysis under the first prong of the internal flight alternative test.

paragraphs.summary: Court concludes RPD was correct in first prong internal flight alternative analysis after reviewing evidence.

propositions.text: Court also disagrees with counsel's arguments on RPD's application of second prong of internal flight alternative test.
propositions.quote: I also do not agree with the arguments that counsel makes for why he believes the RPD erred in the application of the second prong of the internal flight alternative test.

paragraphs.summary: Court rejects counsel's arguments that RPD erred on second prong of internal flight alternative test.

propositions.text: Counsel's reasons for unreasonableness of relocation were not given by Ms. XXXX at hearing.
propositions.quote: At the outset, I note that the reasons given by counsel as to why it would be unreasonable to expect Ms. XXXX and her sons to relocate to one of the internal flight alternatives were not actually reasons given by Ms. XXXX at the hearing.

propositions.text: Ms. XXXX said no safety anywhere in Nigeria due to brother-in-law tracking; no other reasons against relocation.
propositions.quote: When the RPD asked Ms. XXXX if there were any reasons why she and her sons could not relocate to one of the internal flight alternative cities, she said there was no safety for them anywhere in Nigeria because her brother-in-law could track them anywhere in the country. When the RPD asked whether there were any other reasons she could not relocate to one of the internal flight alternative cities, she said no.15

paragraphs.summary: Court notes counsel's reasons for unreasonableness differ from Ms. XXXX's hearing testimony denying other relocation reasons.

propositions.text: Counsel argues indigeneity makes relocation unreasonable; Ms. XXXX expressed no such concern.
propositions.quote: In the appeal memorandum, counsel makes arguments about indigeneity (ethnic majority status) in Nigeria. Ms. XXXX herself expressed no concern about indigeneity being a factor that would make her relocation to any of the internal flight alternative cities unreasonable.

propositions.text: National Documentation shows some indigeneity discrimination but less in big cities like Lagos or Abuja with large non-indigene populations.
propositions.quote: It is true that the National Documentation Package indicates that there is some discrimination based on indigeneity... However, the evidence also indicates that indigene status is less important in big cities such as Lagos or Abuja...

propositions.text: Evidence does not support counsel's argument that discrimination in Abuja would jeopardize Ms. XXXX and sons' safety.
propositions.quote: Therefore, I do not find that the evidence supports counsel's argument that any challenges or discrimination that Ms. XXXX or her sons might face on the basis of being non-indigenes of Abuja that would rise to the level required to place their lives and safety in jeopardy in these cities.

paragraphs.summary: Counsel argues indigeneity discrimination makes relocation unreasonable; court finds evidence does not support this for Abuja.

propositions.text: Counsel argues Ms. XXXX would invariably face ethnic discrimination in employment and medical care.
propositions.quote: I also do not agree with counsel's argument that "invariably" Ms. XXXX would be discriminated against based on ethnic background in terms of employment, medical care, etc.

propositions.text: Ms. XXXX expressed no concern about ethnic discrimination; evidence shows some hiring discrimination in Port Harcourt but not in Abuja or Enugu to jeopardize safety.
propositions.quote: Again, Ms. XXXX expressed no concern about this being the case... the National Documentation Package does not support the argument that Ms. XXXX is likely to experience discrimination in either Abuja or Enugu to such an extent that it would place her or her son's lives and safety in jeopardy.

paragraphs.summary: Counsel argues ethnic discrimination is inevitable; court finds no evidence it would jeopardize safety in Abuja or Enugu.

propositions.text: Counsel argues Ms. XXXX's status as newly single woman makes relocation unreasonable.
propositions.quote: I also do not agree with counsel's arguments based on Ms. XXXX's alleged status as a newly single woman.

propositions.text: Ms. XXXX raised no concerns about making a living or housing as single woman; court doubts credibility of divorce claim but finds no evidence relocation unreasonable.
propositions.quote: Once again, Ms. XXXX raised no concerns in relation to her ability to make a living and find housing as a single woman. I note that I have serious concerns about the credibility of Ms. XXXX claim... Nevertheless... evidence does not establish... unreasonable to expect Ms. XXXX and her sons to relocate to Abuja or Enugu.

paragraphs.summary: Counsel argues single status makes relocation unreasonable; court finds no evidence and doubts divorce claim credibility.

propositions.text: Discrimination against single women more prevalent in northern Nigeria; depends on education and work experience.
propositions.quote: While the evidence in the National Documentation Packages does indicate that single women do experience some discrimination... this discrimination is more prevalent in the northern part of the country... likelihood depends on her particular profile.

propositions.text: Ms. XXXX has education and work experience; evidence shows women often find informal sector jobs like Ms. XXXX did before leaving Nigeria.
propositions.quote: Contrary to counsel's arguments, Ms. XXXX is not lacking in work experience... women often end up finding jobs in the informal sector XXXX XXXX which is the kind of work that Ms. XXXX performed XXXX XXXX before she left Nigeria.

propositions.text: No evidence spouse would refuse financial responsibilities toward sons even if separated.
propositions.quote: Finally, I note that, even if I accepted as true that Ms. XXXX and her spouse have separated, there was no evidence in this case that her spouse would refuse to fulfill his financial responsibilities toward his sons.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds discrimination against single women varies; Ms. XXXX has experience; no evidence spouse would refuse support.

propositions.text: Housing discrimination against female-headed households exists in large Nigerian cities; Ms. XXXX raised no housing concerns for Abuja or Enugu.
propositions.quote: In terms of discrimination in housing, the National Documentation Package does indicate that it is difficult for female-headed households to find housing in large cities in Nigeria... Ms. XXXX did not herself raise any concern about her ability to find housing in either Abuja or Enugu...

paragraphs.summary: Housing discrimination exists but Ms. XXXX raised no concerns about housing in Abuja or Enugu.

propositions.text: Counsel relies on evidence that Nigerian government lacks general support for women in need.
propositions.quote: In terms of access to social services, counsel seeks to rely on a part of the National Documentation Package that indicates that the Nigerian government has no general support for women in need.

propositions.text: Lack of general government support for women is a country-wide issue; no evidence Abuja or Enugu provide less social services than elsewhere.
propositions.quote: In my view, this is a general issue across the country and there is no evidence that Abuja or Enugu provide less in the way of social services than the rest of the country.

paragraphs.summary: Counsel cites lack of government support for women; court finds it a general issue with no less support in Abuja or Enugu.

propositions.text: Counsel argues RPD erred by basing decision on Ms. XXXX's ability to relocate to Canada, citing Utoh case.
propositions.quote: I disagree with counsel that the RPD erred in basing its decision on Ms. XXXX ability to relocate to Canada. Therefore, the Utoh21 case cited by counsel has no relevance to this case.

propositions.text: RPD gave extensive reasons why cultural, religious, linguistic, economic factors do not make relocation unreasonable; did not rest decision on ability to relocate to Canada.
propositions.quote: The RPD gave extensive reasons for why the evidence did not establish that there existed cultural, religious, linguistic, economic or other factors that would make it unreasonable to expect Ms. XXXX to relocate... It did not rest its decision on Ms. XXXX ability to relocate to Canada.

paragraphs.summary: Counsel argues RPD erred relying on relocation to Canada; court finds RPD did not rely on that and gave extensive reasons.

propositions.text: Counsel relies on Okonkwo decision where RPD found claimant safe due to family and English skills, with contradictory reasoning.
propositions.quote: I fail to see the relevance of the Okonkwo22 decision cited by counsel as the facts in that case bear no relationship to this one. In that case, the RPD found that the claimant would be safe in a particular city merely because she had family there...

propositions.text: Okonkwo case facts differ significantly; counsel's reliance on it is unclear.
propositions.quote: None of these are factors in this case. Therefore, it is unclear why counsel seeks to rely upon the decision in the present case.

paragraphs.summary: Counsel cites Okonkwo case; court finds facts differ and counsel's reliance unclear.

propositions.text: Counsel argues RPD had onus to prove viable internal flight alternative in XXXX city.
propositions.quote: In terms of XXXX, I do not agree with counsel that it was the RPD's onus to demonstrate that Ms. XXXX and her sons would have a viable internal flight alternative in that city.

propositions.text: Onus is on Ms. XXXX and sons to prove no viable internal flight alternative, which they failed to do.
propositions.quote: Instead, it was Ms. XXXX and her sons who had the onus of establishing that they did not have a viable internal flight alternative in that city, which they failed to do for all the reasons set out above.

paragraphs.summary: Counsel argues RPD had onus to prove internal flight alternative; court states onus is on Ms. XXXX and sons, which they failed.

propositions.text: The RPD's internal flight alternative finding was not based on speculation as in Loya Dominguez.
propositions.quote: Finally, the RPD's internal flight alternative finding was not based on speculation as was the case in the Loya Dominguez case cited by counsel.

propositions.text: The RPD's conclusions were well supported by evidence in the National Documentation Package for Nigeria.
propositions.quote: The RPD's conclusions were well supported by the evidence contained in the National Documentation Package for Nigeria.

propositions.text: Although Ms. XXXX and her sons may face challenges relocating, these are not significant enough to jeopardize their lives or safety.
propositions.quote: While it is to be expected to Ms. XXXX and her sons may face challenges relocating to a different city in Nigeria, I agree with the RPD that the evidence does not establish that these difficulties will be of such significance as to put their lives and safety in jeopardy, as is required to find a particular internal flight alternative unreasonable.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RPD's internal flight alternative finding was not speculative, was well supported by evidence, and relocation challenges do not jeopardize safety.

propositions.text: The appeal is dismissed and the RPD decision confirmed that appellants are neither Convention refugees nor persons in need of protection.
propositions.quote: For the above reasons, I dismiss the appeal and confirm the decision of the RPD that the Appellants are neither Convention refugees nor persons in need of protection.

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses the appeal and confirms the RPD decision that appellants are not refugees or in need of protection.
